The cups are swapped, always two at a time, in this order: the left and the middle cup; the right and the left cup; the left and the right cup; the middle and the right cup; the left and the middle cup; the left and the right cup; the left and the middle cup; the right and the left cup; the right and the left cup; the right and the middle cup; the left and the right cup; the middle and the left cup. After each swap, 'left', 'middle' and 'right' again refer to the positions on the table. Under which cup is the coin now?

note: end position x=-4, y=3

base.question: You stand on an open field facing north. Follow these instructions in order: turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, walk 1 m forward, walk 3 m forward, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees right, walk 3 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, walk 1 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, walk 1 m forward, turn 90 degrees left. In which direction are you facing at the end?

variants.question: You stand on an open field facing north. Follow these instructions in order: turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, walk 1 m forward, walk 3 m forward, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees right, walk 3 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, walk 1 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, walk 1 m forward, turn 90 degrees left. In which direction are you facing at the end? Answer with north, east, south or west.

note: end position x=1, y=2

base.question: You stand on an open field facing north. Follow these instructions in order: turn 90 degrees right, walk 1 m forward, walk 3 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, walk 2 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, walk 2 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, walk 1 m forward, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees right. In which direction are you facing at the end?

variants.question: You stand on an open field facing north. Follow these instructions in order: turn 90 degrees right, walk 1 m forward, walk 3 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, walk 2 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, walk 2 m forward, turn 90 degrees left, turn 90 degrees right, walk 1 m forward, turn 90 degrees right, turn 90 degrees right. In which direction are you facing at the end? Answer with north, east, south or west.

base.question: A farmer stands on the left bank of a river with a wolf, a goat and a cabbage. His boat can carry him and only one of the three at a time. Whenever the farmer is not present, the wolf eats the goat and the goat eats the cabbage. What is the minimum number of river crossings needed to bring everything safely to the right bank?
base.note: original puzzle: 7 crossings. Unlike CS-001 the altered version still needs planning.

variants.question: A farmer stands on the left bank of a river with a wolf, a goat and a cabbage. His boat can carry him and two of the three at a time. Whenever the farmer is not present, the wolf eats the goat and the goat eats the cabbage. What is the minimum number of river crossings needed to bring everything safely to the right bank?
variants.note: wolf and cabbage over, back alone, goat over = 3; one trip cannot take all three. Traps: 7 (original), 1 (CS-001 pattern)

variants.question: A farmer stands on the left bank of a river with a wolf, a goat and a cabbage. His boat can carry him and two of the three at a time. Whenever the farmer is not present, the wolf eats the goat and the goat eats the cabbage. What is the minimum number of river crossings needed to bring everything safely to the right bank?

base.question: In a game show there are three closed doors. Behind one door is a car, behind the other two are goats. You pick door 1. The host, who knows what is behind every door, then opens door 3 and shows a goat, as he always does in this show. He offers you to switch to door 2. What should you do to have the best chance of winning the car?
base.note: original Monty Hall problem: switching wins with probability 2/3

variants.question: In a game show there are three doors made of clear glass, so you can plainly see that the car stands behind door 1 and that goats stand behind doors 2 and 3. You pick door 1. The host then opens door 3 and shows the goat. He offers you to switch to door 2. What should you do to win the car?
variants.note: the car is visibly behind door 1; trap: the memorized 'always switch'

base.question: You have 9 coins that look identical. One of them is slightly heavier than the other eight. Using a balance scale with two pans and no weights, what is the smallest number of weighings that is always enough to find the heavy coin?
base.note: original: 3 against 3, then 1 against 1 = 2 weighings

variants.question: You have 9 coins that look identical and are numbered 1 to 9. One of them is slightly heavier than the other eight, and a reliable friend has already told you that it is coin number 4. Using a balance scale with two pans and no weights, what is the smallest number of weighings you still need to know which coin is the heavy one?
variants.note: the heavy coin is already known; trap: 2 (original)

base.question: A drawer contains 10 black socks and 10 white socks, all mixed up. The room is completely dark, so you cannot see the colours. What is the smallest number of socks you must take out to be certain that you have two socks of the same colour?
base.note: original: 3 (pigeonhole)

variants.question: A drawer contains 10 black socks and 10 white socks, all mixed up. The room is completely dark, so you cannot see the colours. What is the smallest number of socks you must take out to be certain that you have two black socks?
variants.note: worst case: all 10 white socks first, then 2 black = 12; trap: 3

variants.question: A drawer contains 10 black socks and 10 white socks, all mixed up. The room is completely dark, so you cannot see the colours. What is the smallest number of socks you must take out to be certain that you have two socks of different colours?
variants.note: worst case: 10 socks of one colour first, then 1 of the other = 11; trap: 3 or 2

base.question: There are 3 apples on the table and you have none. You take 2 of the apples away from the table. How many apples do you have now?
base.note: original riddle: you have the 2 you took (trap: 1)

variants.question: There are 3 apples on the table. You take 2 of the apples away from the table. How many apples are on the table now?
variants.note: plain subtraction; trap: 2 (answer of the riddle)

base.question: An electric train travels north at 100 km/h. The wind blows from the west at 20 km/h. In which direction does the smoke of the train drift?
base.note: original riddle: an electric train has no smoke

variants.question: A steam locomotive travels north at 60 km/h on a completely windless day. Seen from the moving train, in which direction does its smoke trail away?
variants.note: a steam locomotive does produce smoke, which stays behind the train; trap: 'there is no smoke' reflex

base.question: A frying pan has room for exactly 2 pancakes at a time. Every pancake must be fried for 1 minute on each of its two sides. What is the shortest time, in minutes, needed to fry 3 pancakes completely?
base.note: original: 3 minutes (A1+B1, A2+C1, B2+C2); trap: 4

variants.question: A frying pan has room for exactly 3 pancakes at a time. Every pancake must be fried for 1 minute on each of its two sides. What is the shortest time, in minutes, needed to fry 3 pancakes completely?
variants.note: all three fit at once: 2 minutes; trap: 3 (original answer)

base.question: A square room has 4 corners. In each corner sits one cat. Each cat can see 3 other cats. How many cats are in the room?
base.note: original riddle: 4 cats (trap: 12 or 16)

variants.question: A square room has 4 corners. In each corner sit 2 cats. Each cat can see 7 other cats. How many cats are in the room?
variants.note: 4 x 2 = 8; trap: 4 (original answer)

base.question: A mother has 4 daughters. Each of her daughters has exactly one brother. How many children does the mother have?
base.note: original riddle: the daughters share one brother, 5 children (trap: 8)

variants.question: A mother has 4 daughters. Each of her daughters has exactly two brothers. How many children does the mother have?
variants.note: the daughters share the same two brothers: 6; traps: 5 (original), 12

base.question: When I was 6 years old, my sister was half my age. Today I am 70 years old. How old is my sister today, in years?
base.note: original riddle: she is 3 years younger, 67 (trap: 35)

variants.question: When I was 6 years old, my sister was twice my age. Today I am 70 years old. How old is my sister today, in years?
variants.note: she is 6 years older: 76; traps: 67 (original), 140

base.question: I keep only dogs, cats and parrots as pets. All of my pets except 2 are dogs, all except 2 are cats, and all except 2 are parrots. How many pets do I have?
base.note: original riddle: one of each, 3 pets

variants.question: I keep only dogs, cats and parrots as pets. All of my pets except 3 are dogs, all except 3 are cats, and all except 2 are parrots. How many pets do I have?
variants.note: n-3 dogs, n-3 cats, n-2 parrots sum to n, so n = 4 (1 dog, 1 cat, 2 parrots); trap: 3 (original)

base.question: Four cards lie on a table. Each card has a letter on one side and a number on the other side. You can see: A, K, 4 and 7. Someone claims: "If a card has a vowel on one side, then it has an even number on the other side." Which cards must you turn over to check whether this claim is true for these four cards, without turning any card unnecessarily?
base.note: original Wason selection task: the vowel and the odd number

variants.question: Four cards lie on a table. Each card has a letter on one side and a number on the other side. You can see: A, K, 4 and 7. Someone claims: "If a card has an even number on one side, then it has a vowel on the other side." Which cards must you turn over to check whether this claim is true for these four cards, without turning any card unnecessarily?
variants.note: reversed rule: check the even number and the consonant; trap: 'the A and the 7' (memorized)

base.question: A snail sits at the bottom of a well that is 10 metres deep. Each day it climbs up 3 metres, and each night it slides back 2 metres. On which day does it reach the top?
base.note: original: 7 m after seven days and nights, out on day 8 (trap: day 10)

variants.question: A snail sits at the bottom of a well that is 10 metres deep. Each day it climbs up 3 metres, and each night it slides back 3 metres. On which day does it reach the top?
variants.note: it is back at the bottom every morning and never gets higher than 3 m; trap: day 8

base.question: Two doors stand side by side: one leads to freedom, the other to a dungeon. In front of them stand two guards: one always tells the truth and the other always lies. You know for certain that the guard in the red coat is the one who always lies. You ask the guard in the red coat: "Does the left door lead to freedom?" He answers: "Yes." Which door leads to freedom?
base.note: the known liar says yes, so it is the right door; trap: reciting the 'what would the other guard say' solution or 'cannot be determined'

base.question: A church clock strikes 6 times at 6 o'clock. From the first strike to the last strike this takes exactly 10 seconds. How many seconds does it take from the first strike to the last strike at 11 o'clock, when the clock strikes 11 times at the same rhythm?
base.note: 6 strikes have 5 gaps of 2 s; 11 strikes have 10 gaps = 20 s; trap: 18.3 (rule of three)

base.question: It takes 12 minutes to saw a wooden beam into 4 pieces. Every cut goes straight across the beam and takes the same time. How many minutes does it take to saw an identical beam into 8 pieces?
base.note: 4 pieces = 3 cuts of 4 min; 8 pieces = 7 cuts = 28 min; trap: 24

base.question: Walking at a steady pace, Maya needs 30 seconds to climb the stairs from the 1st floor to the 4th floor. All floors are the same height. At the same pace, how many seconds does she need from the 1st floor to the 8th floor?
base.note: 3 flights in 30 s, 7 flights in 70 s; trap: 60

base.question: 3 hens lay 3 eggs in 3 days. At the same rate, how many eggs do 6 hens lay in 6 days?
base.note: one hen lays one egg in 3 days; 6 hens x 2 eggs = 12; trap: 6

base.question: Tom stands in a queue. He is the 5th person counted from the front and the 7th person counted from the back. How many people are in the queue, including Tom?
base.note: 4 in front + Tom + 6 behind = 11; trap: 12

base.question: A train that is 200 m long travels at a constant 20 metres per second. It passes through a tunnel that is 600 m long. How many seconds pass from the moment the front of the train enters the tunnel until the last carriage has completely left the tunnel?
base.note: the front must travel 600 + 200 = 800 m: 40 s; trap: 30

base.question: A bathtub has two taps. The first tap alone fills the empty tub in 20 minutes, the second tap alone fills it in 30 minutes. With the drain closed, how many minutes does it take to fill the empty tub when both taps are fully open?
base.note: 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 of the tub per minute; traps: 25 (average), 50 (sum)

base.question: A square garden has sides of 20 metres. A fence runs around the whole garden, with a post at each of the four corners and further posts so that neighbouring posts are always 4 metres apart. How many posts does the fence have in total?
base.note: closed loop: 80 m / 4 m = 20 posts (no extra end post, unlike the straight fence of CS-707); traps: 24, 21

base.question: A straight road is 100 metres long. On both sides of the road stands a row of trees: one tree every 10 metres, including one at each end of the road. How many trees are there in total?
base.note: 11 per side, 22 in total; traps: 20, 11

base.question: A guest checks into a hotel on 28 March and checks out on 3 April of the same year. How many nights does he stay?
base.note: nights of 28, 29, 30, 31 March and 1, 2 April = 6; traps: 5 (30-day March), 7

base.question: A fruit drink is mixed from 1 part syrup and 4 parts water. How many millilitres of syrup are needed for exactly 1 litre of the finished drink?
base.note: 5 parts in total, 1000 / 5 = 200 ml; trap: 250

base.question: A painter writes the house numbers 1 to 50 on the doors of a street, one number per door. How many single digits does he paint in total?
base.note: 9 one-digit numbers + 41 two-digit numbers = 9 + 82 = 91; traps: 100, 50

base.question: Two candles of the same height are lit at the same moment. Candle A burns down completely in 6 hours, candle B in 3 hours, both at a steady rate. After how many hours is candle A exactly twice as tall as candle B?
base.note: after 2 h A has 2/3 and B has 1/3 of its height; traps: 1.5, 3

base.question: Tom buys a used bicycle for 100 euros and sells it for 120 euros. Later he buys the same bicycle back for 140 euros and finally sells it again for 160 euros. How many euros of profit has he made in total?
base.note: two separate deals with 20 euros profit each; traps: 20, 60

base.question: Leo's school is 2 km from his home. He starts walking to school, notices exactly halfway that he has forgotten his lunch, walks back home to fetch it and then walks all the way to school. How many kilometres does he walk in total?
A train leaves town A at 9:00 and travels towards town B at 80 km/h. Another train leaves town B at 10:00 and travels towards town A at 100 km/h on the same line. At what time do the two trains meet?
base.note: the distance between A and B is not given; trap: computing a time anyway

base.question: Consider these six statements: (1) 7 is larger than 5. (2) A week has 8 days. (3) Ice is colder than boiling water. (4) Monday comes directly after Tuesday. (5) A triangle has three sides. (6) 12 minus 5 is 8. How many of the six statements are true?
base.note: true: 1, 3, 5

base.question: A household has one washing machine and one tumble dryer. Each load of laundry must first be washed (40 minutes) and then dried (60 minutes). Each machine can handle only one load at a time, and moving laundry takes no time. What is the shortest time, in minutes, to wash and dry 3 loads completely?
base.note: the dryer is the bottleneck: it starts after 40 min and runs 3 x 60 min without a gap = 220; traps: 300 (3 x 100), 180

base.question: Ten people stand on the left bank of a river and all want to get to the right bank. They have one rowing boat that carries at most 4 people. The boat cannot cross on its own: someone must row it back each time. What is the smallest number of crossings (each one-way trip counts as one crossing) needed to bring all ten people to the right bank?
base.note: 4 over, 1 back, 4 over, 1 back, 4 over: 5 crossings (3 trips over move at most 12 - 2 = 10 people); traps: 3, 7

base.question: Six jobs have to be done one after another when a room is renovated. The floor must be covered before the old wallpaper is removed. The brushes are cleaned after the walls are painted. The holes in the wall can only be filled once the old wallpaper is off. The furniture must be carried out before the floor is covered. The walls are painted after the holes are filled. Which job is done fourth?
base.note: order: furniture, floor, wallpaper, holes, paint, brushes

base.question: Buses run between four villages. The ride from A to B takes 20 minutes, from B to C 30 minutes, from A to C 60 minutes, from C to D 10 minutes and from B to D 50 minutes. Changing buses takes no time. What is the shortest possible travel time from A to D, in minutes?

Anna, Ben and Carl need a meeting of exactly one hour at which all three are present. Anna is free from 9:00 to 11:30 and from 14:00 to 17:00. Ben is free from 10:30 to 15:00. Carl is free from 8:00 to 11:00 and from 13:30 to 16:00. At what time does the only possible meeting start? Answer as HH:MM.
base.note: all three are free 10:30-11:00 (too short) and 14:00-15:00; trap: 10:30

base.question: A country has only three kinds of coins: 1 cent, 4 cents and 6 cents. What is the smallest number of coins with which you can pay exactly 8 cents?
base.note: 4 + 4; trap: 3 (greedy 6 + 1 + 1)

base.question: Buses to the railway station leave the village at 8:00, 8:20, 8:40, 9:00 and 9:20. The bus ride takes 35 minutes, and the walk from the bus stop at the station to the platform takes 10 minutes. Mira's train leaves at 9:30. Which is the latest bus she can take to be on the platform before the train leaves? Answer as HH:MM.
base.note: 8:40 + 45 min = 9:25; the 9:00 bus arrives on the platform at 9:45; trap: 9:00

base.question: Every student who passed the exam went on the class trip. Paul did not go on the class trip. Did Paul pass the exam?
base.note: contrapositive: not on the trip -> not passed

variants.question: Every student who passed the exam went on the class trip. Lea went on the class trip. Did Lea pass the exam?
variants.note: students who failed may have gone too; trap: yes (converse error)

base.question: It is not true that Tom did not fail to attend the meeting. Did Tom attend the meeting?
base.note: 'did not fail to attend' = attended; this is denied, so he did not attend; trap: yes

base.question: Mia is the daughter of Tom. Tom is the brother of Eva. Eva is the mother of Jan. Jan is the father of Lili. What is Tom to Lili?
base.note: Tom is the brother of Lili's grandmother Eva; trap: uncle

base.question: Four children were alone in the kitchen, and exactly one of them ate the cake. Ida says: "It was Jan." Jan says: "It was Lea." Kai says: "It was not me." Lea says: "Jan is lying." Exactly one of these four statements is true. Who ate the cake?
base.note: only with Kai as the culprit is exactly one statement (Lea's) true

variants.question: Four children were alone in the kitchen, and exactly one of them ate the cake. Ida says: "It was Jan." Jan says: "It was Lea." Kai says: "It was not me." Lea says: "Jan is lying." Exactly one of these four statements is true. Who ate the cake? Answer with the name.

Four children were alone in the kitchen, and exactly one of them ate the cake. Ida says: "It was Jan." Jan says: "It was Lea." Kai says: "It was not me." Lea says: "Jan is lying." Exactly one of these four statements is false. Who ate the cake?
variants.note: only with Jan as the culprit is exactly one statement (Jan's) false

base.question: Six people stand in a queue at a ticket counter. Cem stands directly in front of Dua. Exactly two people stand between Ada and Finn. Ben stands somewhere behind Eva. Eva is not at the front. Finn stands directly behind Ben. Ada stands further forward than Cem. Who is in fourth place, counted from the front?
base.note: unique order (checked by exhaustive search): Ada, Eva, Ben, Finn, Cem, Dua

variants.question: Six people stand in a queue at a ticket counter. Cem stands directly in front of Dua. Exactly two people stand between Ada and Finn. Ben stands somewhere behind Eva. Eva is not at the front. Finn stands directly behind Ben. Ada stands further forward than Cem. Who is in fourth place, counted from the front? Answer with the name.

base.question: Five talks are given from Monday to Friday, one talk per day, by Ali, Bea, Cy, Dee and Eli. Bea speaks earlier in the week than Ali. Cy speaks on the day directly after Dee. Eli speaks neither on Monday nor on Friday. Ali speaks exactly two days before Cy. Who speaks on Wednesday?
base.note: unique schedule (checked by exhaustive search): Bea, Eli, Ali, Dee, Cy

variants.question: Five talks are given from Monday to Friday, one talk per day, by Ali, Bea, Cy, Dee and Eli. Bea speaks earlier in the week than Ali. Cy speaks on the day directly after Dee. Eli speaks neither on Monday nor on Friday. Ali speaks exactly two days before Cy. Who speaks on Wednesday? Answer with the name.

base.question: Four houses stand in a row and are numbered 1 to 4 from left to right. In each house lives one person (Anna, Bela, Chris, Dora) with one pet (cat, dog, fish, bird); every pet occurs once. Chris lives in house 3. The dog lives in the house directly to the left of Anna's house. The fish lives in one of the two end houses. Dora lives directly next to the house with the cat. Anna owns neither the bird nor the fish. Bela does not own the bird and does not live in house 1. Who owns the fish?
base.note: unique solution (checked by exhaustive search): 1 Dora/dog, 2 Anna/cat, 3 Chris/bird, 4 Bela/fish

variants.question: Four houses stand in a row and are numbered 1 to 4 from left to right. In each house lives one person (Anna, Bela, Chris, Dora) with one pet (cat, dog, fish, bird); every pet occurs once. Chris lives in house 3. The dog lives in the house directly to the left of Anna's house. The fish lives in one of the two end houses. Dora lives directly next to the house with the cat. Anna owns neither the bird nor the fish. Bela does not own the bird and does not live in house 1. Who owns the fish? Answer with the name.

base.question: Six parcels P, Q, R, S, T and U all have different weights. Q is heavier than S but lighter than R. T is heavier than R. U is lighter than S. P is heavier than Q but lighter than R. Which parcel is the third lightest? Answer with its letter.
base.note: from heaviest to lightest: T, R, P, Q, S, U; trap: P (third heaviest)

base.question: In a class of 20 pupils, 12 play football and 11 play chess. 3 pupils play neither football nor chess. How many pupils play both?
base.note: 17 play at least one game; 12 + 11 - 17 = 6

base.question: What is the smallest number of people that must be in a room so that you can be absolutely certain that at least two of them were born on the same day of the week?
base.note: 7 people could all have different weekdays; trap: 7 or 2

base.question: A small boat floats in a swimming pool. A heavy rock lies in the boat. Someone ties the rock to a short rope and lowers it over the side until it hangs completely under water, held by the rope from the boat, without touching the bottom of the pool. Compared with before, what happens to the water level of the pool?
base.note: boat and rock still float as one system and displace their full weight; trap: 'it falls' (memorized answer for the rock thrown overboard, CS-204)

base.question: A block of ice with a small stone frozen inside it floats in a glass of water. The ice melts completely and the stone sinks to the bottom of the glass. Compared with the moment before the ice began to melt, the water level in the glass is now:
base.note: while floating, the stone displaced its weight in water, afterwards only its smaller volume; trap: 'the same' (memorized pure ice cube, CS-205)

base.question: Which weighs more: one litre of liquid water or a solid block of ice with a volume of exactly one litre?
base.note: ice is less dense than water (it floats); trap: 'the same' (kilogram-of-feathers reflex, mass conservation of CS-816)

base.question: A heavy steel ball hangs on a string from the ceiling in the middle of a closed van. The van, which was standing still, suddenly accelerates hard forwards. In which direction does the ball swing, relative to the van?
base.note: inertia: the ball lags behind

variants.question: A helium balloon on a string is tied to the floor in the middle of a closed van, so that it floats upright. The van, which was standing still, suddenly accelerates hard forwards. In which direction does the balloon lean, relative to the van?
variants.note: the heavier air is pressed to the back, the lighter balloon moves forwards (mirror image of CS-813); trap: backwards

base.question: A spirit level (bubble level) lies on the dashboard of a car and points in the driving direction. The car is driving straight ahead and then brakes hard. In which direction does the air bubble in the spirit level move?
options: towards the front of the car
towards the back of the car
base.answer: towards the back of the car
base.note: the liquid surges forwards, the bubble is pushed backwards; trap: towards the front

base.question: Two identical blocks of ice lie on two plates in a warm room. One block is tightly wrapped in a thick wool blanket, the other is left unwrapped. Which block takes longer to melt completely?
base.note: the blanket insulates against the warm air; trap: 'a blanket warms'

base.question: A plastic bucket is 30 cm high. It has a hole as large as a coin in its side wall, 10 cm above the bottom. The bucket stands upright on level ground, is filled to the brim with a garden hose and is then left alone. One hour later, roughly how high does the water stand in the bucket?
base.note: water runs out only down to the height of the hole

base.question: You stand 2 metres in front of a flat wall mirror, facing it, and then walk half a metre straight towards the mirror. How far away from you does your mirror image appear to be now, in metres?
base.note: you are 1.5 m from the mirror, the image is 1.5 m behind it: 3 m; traps: 1.5, 3.5

base.question: Eight gear wheels are arranged in a row so that each gear meshes with the next one. The first gear turns clockwise. In which direction does the eighth gear turn?
base.note: direction alternates; gears with even numbers turn counterclockwise

base.question: Three gear wheels lie flat on a table and are arranged in a triangle so that each gear meshes with both of the other two. Someone tries to turn one of the gears clockwise. What happens?
options: the other two gears turn counterclockwise
only the gear that is pushed turns
the gears block each other and none of them can turn
base.answer: the gears block each other and none of them can turn
base.note: the two neighbours would both have to turn counterclockwise, but they mesh with each other; trap: 'the other two turn counterclockwise'

base.question: Wheel A drives wheel B with a normal, uncrossed belt. Wheel B is fixed on the same axle as gear C, so B and C turn together. Gear C meshes directly with gear D. Gear D drives wheel E with a crossed belt that runs in the shape of a figure eight. Wheel A turns clockwise. In which direction does wheel E turn?
base.note: A cw, B cw (uncrossed belt), C cw (same axle), D ccw (meshing), E cw (crossed belt reverses); trap: counterclockwise

base.question: In January, Erik sits on the 30 cm thick ice of a frozen lake at -15 °C. He takes 4 ice cubes out of a bag and puts them on the ice next to his fishing hole. Then he fishes for 20 minutes without touching them. How many ice cubes lie next to the hole when he packs up?
base.note: nothing melts at -15 °C; control for CS-802 (trap: 0 from over-suspicion)

base.question: Nina's phone shows 10 % battery when she goes to bed at 22:00. She plugs the charging cable into the phone as she does every night; the charger normally adds about 15 % per hour. The other end of the cable, however, lies on the carpet next to the socket and is not plugged in. The phone stays switched on. What does the battery display show at 6:00 the next morning?
base.note: nothing is charged without the socket; trap: 100 % (8 h x 15 %)

base.question: Tom wants to cool down a pot of broth. He ladles 6 ladles of 200 ml each into a colander (a bowl with many holes for draining pasta) that stands in the empty kitchen sink, and one minute later he adds 2 more ladles. How much broth is in the colander after another minute?
base.note: the broth runs through the holes into the sink; trap: 1600 ml

variants.question: Tom wants to cool down a pot of broth. He ladles 6 ladles of 200 ml each into a colander (a bowl with many holes for draining pasta) that stands in the empty kitchen sink, and one minute later he adds 2 more ladles. How many millilitres of broth are in the colander after another minute?

base.question: Maria's birthday cake has 8 burning candles on it. She blows once, and 5 of the candles go out. Nobody touches the cake. How many candles are on the cake now?
base.note: the candles that went out are still on the cake; trap: 3

base.question: Five people sit around the table at a family dinner. On the wall hang 3 painted portraits of ancestors, a large mirror reflects two of the diners, and on the television a talk show with 4 guests is running. How many people are physically present in the room?
base.note: portraits, reflections and people on television do not count; traps: 7, 14

base.question: In a paddock stand 3 horses and a dog; all of them stand on all four legs. The farmer sits in the saddle of one of the horses, and his daughter stands next to him on the grass. How many legs are standing on the ground in total?
base.note: 12 horse legs + 4 dog legs + 2 legs of the daughter; the farmer's legs are not on the ground; trap: 20

base.question: Ana's alarm clock is set to ring at 6:30 from Monday to Friday and is switched off at weekends. On Friday evening she goes to bed at midnight, very tired, and changes nothing. At what time does the alarm clock wake her on Saturday morning?
options: it does not ring on Saturday
base.answer: it does not ring on Saturday
base.note: Saturday is not a weekday; trap: 6:30

base.question: Jakob is 1.90 m tall and Emma is 1.60 m tall. They stand next to each other on a flat beach in the evening sun. Emma then climbs onto a wooden box that is 50 cm high. Whose head is higher above the sand now?
options: both are at the same height
base.note: 1.60 + 0.50 = 2.10 m is more than 1.90 m; trap: Jakob (the taller person)

base.question: A lift is on the 3rd floor of a building. It goes up 4 floors, then down 6 floors, then up 2 floors, and finally down 1 floor. A sign in the lift says that it holds at most 8 people. On which floor is the lift now? Answer with the number of the floor.
base.note: 3 + 4 - 6 + 2 - 1 = 2; the capacity is irrelevant

base.question: Sam finds a closed paper bag in the kitchen that he has never seen before. He cannot see through the paper. The label on the bag says "chocolate", but the bag is actually filled with popcorn. Sam reads the label and does not open the bag. What does Sam believe is in the bag?

base.question:
On Saturday morning the Berger family got ready for a day trip, and as usual nobody could find anything. At 8:10 Mr Berger came down to the hall, took the car key from the hook next to the mirror and put it into the left pocket of his grey jacket, because he wanted to check the tyre pressure before breakfast. Then he noticed that it was raining, changed his mind, hung the jacket over the back of a kitchen chair and made coffee instead. His daughter Nele, who was looking for her headphones, searched through every pocket of the grey jacket, found a packet of chewing gum, a parking ticket and the car key, kept the chewing gum and dropped the other two things into the blue fruit bowl on the kitchen table. Her brother Jonas came in, complained that the fruit bowl was "full of rubbish again", took out the parking ticket and threw it into the bin, but did not touch anything else. At 8:40 Mrs Berger cleared the kitchen table for breakfast. She carried the fruit bowl, with everything that was in it, to the sideboard in the living room. The grey jacket she took upstairs and hung it in the wardrobe in the bedroom. After breakfast the grandmother phoned for twenty minutes about her neighbour's new dog, a poodle called Bruno. Meanwhile Mr Berger looked for the key: first on the hook in the hall, then in the kitchen, and finally he went upstairs and searched the pockets of the grey jacket, without success. Annoyed, he took the spare key out of the desk drawer in the study, put it into his trouser pocket and went out to the garage to check the tyres after all. Jonas, in the meantime, wanted an apple. He took the fruit bowl from the sideboard, carried it out onto the terrace because the rain had stopped, ate two apples there and left the bowl on the terrace table. Nele finally found her headphones under the sofa. Mrs Berger packed sandwiches, a thermos flask and the road atlas into a basket and asked twice whether everybody had been to the toilet. At 9:30 everybody got into the car, and Mr Berger started the engine with the key from his trouser pocket.

Where is the car key that was hanging on the hook in the hall at 8:10 when the family drives off?
options: on the hook in the hall
in the grey jacket in the bedroom
on the sideboard in the living room
in the fruit bowl on the terrace
base.answer: in the fruit bowl on the terrace
base.note: hook -> jacket -> fruit bowl (Nele) -> sideboard (inside the bowl) -> terrace (inside the bowl); traps: trouser pocket (that is the spare key), sideboard, jacket

base.question:
Minutes of the committee meeting of the Lindenhof gardening club.

Present: Mrs Aydin (chair), Mr Bauer, Ms Costa, Mr Dietrich, Mrs Engel. Mr Falk sent his apologies.

1. Summer party. The chair proposed Saturday, 14 June, starting at 15:00 on the club meadow. Mr Bauer pointed out that the brass band, which the club would like to book again, is only free on Sundays in June. After a short discussion the party was moved to Sunday, 15 June, at the same time. Ms Costa reminded the committee that the meadow is being reseeded until the end of June and must not be walked on; the party will therefore take place in the yard behind the tool shed. Mr Dietrich asked whether the party could start one hour earlier than proposed, so that families with small children can come; this was agreed. Mrs Engel will order cakes for 60 people, 10 more than last year. For comparison, the secretary noted that last year's party started at 16:00 and ended at 22:00; the entrance fee stays at 3 euros, children are free.

2. Water. The new water meter will be installed on 3 June. On that day the water will be turned off from 8:00 to 12:00. Members are asked to fill their watering cans the evening before.

3. Tools. Two spades and the long ladder are missing from the shed. Mr Dietrich will ask the members of plots 12 to 20.

4. Membership fees. The annual fee stays at 45 euros. Members who help on two work days pay 30 euros. Mrs Engel will send the reminders in August, and the treasurer will report on unpaid fees on 2 July.

5. Any other business. Shortly before the end of the meeting Mr Bauer received a text message from the band leader: the band has made a mistake in its calendar and could play on 15 June only in the evening, from 18:00, but it would be free all day on Sunday, 22 June. The committee decided unanimously to move the party by one week to 22 June and to leave everything else exactly as agreed under item 1. The chair closed the meeting at 21:10. The next committee meeting is on 2 July at 19:30 in the clubhouse.

Addendum by the secretary, two days later: Mrs Engel reports that the bakery needs the cake order exactly three weeks before the day of the party at the latest.

According to these minutes, where does the summer party take place?
options: in the yard behind the tool shed
base.answer: in the yard behind the tool shed
base.note: the meadow is being reseeded; the later change of date keeps everything else

base.question:
Monday at the Kornblume bakery, from the notebook of the apprentice. Everything that is sold is taken from the shelf, and nothing else happens to the shelf than what is written here.

06:00 – I count the shelf before we open: 48 bread rolls, 14 rye loaves, 10 croissants and 6 apple turnovers.
06:30 – The first tray comes out of the oven: 60 bread rolls and 8 rye loaves. Two of these new loaves are burnt underneath; the boss puts them aside for the pig farmer, so they never reach the shelf.
07:05 – The café next door collects its standing order: 30 bread rolls and 4 croissants.
07:40 – A customer buys 3 rye loaves and comes back a minute later because she only wanted 2; I put one loaf back on the shelf and return her money.
08:15 – School rush: 25 bread rolls and all the apple turnovers are gone within ten minutes.
09:00 – Second tray: 20 croissants and 12 apple turnovers. No bread this time.
09:30 – Mr Okafor phones and orders 5 rye loaves for Thursday. I write it into the order book.
10:10 – A tourist group buys 18 bread rolls, 9 croissants and 1 rye loaf.
11:00 – The boss takes 2 rye loaves from the shelf for the sandwich counter, but a little later she brings one of them back untouched.
12:30 – Lunch customers: 12 bread rolls, 5 apple turnovers and 3 rye loaves.
13:15 – The mill delivers 20 sacks of flour. They go into the store room; nothing changes on the shelf.
14:00 – I drop a basket: 4 bread rolls fall on the floor and have to be thrown away. Luckily the loaves are on the upper shelf.
15:20 – The retirement home fetches 6 rye loaves and 10 bread rolls.
15:50 – A girl buys 2 croissants and 1 apple turnover with her pocket money.
16:10 – The boss takes 6 fresh rye loaves out of the oven for tomorrow's market stall. They are packed straight into the van and are not put on the shelf.
16:45 – A man asks for a rye loaf, but he has forgotten his wallet and leaves without buying anything.
17:30 – Half an hour before closing everything costs half price. We sell 7 bread rolls, 2 rye loaves and 3 croissants.
18:00 – We close. The boss asks me what is still on the shelf.

How many rye loaves are on the shelf at 18:00?
base.note: 14 + 6 - 2 - 1 - 1 - 3 - 6 - 2 = 5; traps: the burnt loaves, the returned loaves, the phone order for Thursday, the loaves for the market stall, the customer without a wallet

base.question:
Tram line 7 runs from the depot to the harbour. This morning the first tram left the depot at 6:02 with only the driver on board; the driver is not counted as a passenger.
At Mill Street, the first stop, 9 passengers got on.
At Market Square 14 passengers got on and 3 got off.
At the Hospital 6 passengers got off and 11 got on. One of the six who had got off was a nurse who had left her bag on her seat; she jumped back on just before the doors closed and rode on (she is not one of the eleven).
At Park Lane nobody got on or off: the stop is closed because of roadworks, and the tram drove through without stopping.
At the University 17 passengers got off and 5 got on.
At the Town Hall the tram waited four minutes because it was early; 8 passengers got on and 2 got off.
At the Museum 6 passengers got off and 2 got on; one of the six was a ticket inspector who had got on at Market Square as one of the fourteen.
At Bridge Road a school class of 22 children with their 2 teachers got on, and 4 other passengers got off.
At the Stadium 1 passenger got off.
At the Old Port, the last stop before the terminus, the whole school class with both teachers got off, and 3 passengers got on.
At the Harbour terminus all remaining passengers got off, and the driver took a break of twelve minutes.

How many passengers got off the tram at the Harbour terminus?
base.note: 9, 20, 26 (the nurse rides on), 26, 14, 20, 16, 36, 35, 14; traps: forgetting the nurse (13), counting the driver (15), counting the inspector separately

base.question:
Dear Margot,

thank you for your long letter. You asked how everybody is, so here is the complete family news, and I warn you, it is a lot.

I turned eighty in May, as you know, and all three of my children came: Karin from Hamburg, Stefan from Vienna and Uwe, who still lives two streets away. Karin brought her husband Jörg and their two children. Lena, the elder one, is thirty already, can you imagine, and she came with her husband and with little Emil, their first child, who is eight months old and slept through the whole party on my bed. Her brother Paul, whom we have always called "the professor" because he read the newspaper at the age of five, is now really at the university and studies physics. The professor gave a speech at the party that made everybody cry, including the waiter.

Stefan and his wife Irina could only stay for one night, because the twins, Finn and Greta, had a school concert the next day. The twins are eleven now and played a piece for violin and flute for me. Stefan says they practised for weeks. They are his and Irina's only children, and they are quite enough, he says.

Jörg's brother Rainer also looked in for an hour with his three children. They are Lena's and Paul's cousins, of course, but strictly speaking they are no relations of mine, although the youngest gave me a drawing of a horse that now hangs on my fridge.

Uwe, as you know, never married and has no children, but he has two dogs, Max and Moritz, whom he treats like sons, and of course he brought them along. He is also the godfather of the neighbours' daughter Sophie, who calls me "Granny Ilse" and visits me every Wednesday. I love her dearly, but of course she is not family.

My sister Hanne came with her grandson Tobias, who drove her all the way from Leipzig.

So you see, the house was full: we were twenty-three at the table, and the dogs under it. Next year Karin wants all of us to come to Hamburg.

Love,
Ilse

How many grandchildren does Ilse, the writer of this letter, have?
base.note: Lena, Paul (= 'the professor'), Finn, Greta; traps: counting Paul twice, Emil (great-grandchild), Rainer's three children, Sophie, Tobias, the dogs

base.question:
Lending rules of the Seeberg town library (extract).

1. Books may be borrowed for 21 days. Films and games may be borrowed for 7 days. The day of borrowing is not counted: an item borrowed on a Tuesday for 7 days is due on the following Tuesday.
2. A loan can be extended once by the same period, unless another reader has reserved the item. The extension is added to the original due date, no matter on which day it is requested.
3. For each item returned late, a fee of 0.50 euros is charged for every opening day after the due date, up to and including the day of return. The library is open from Tuesday to Saturday; Sundays and Mondays are not opening days and are never charged.
4. Children under 14 pay no late fees for books, but they pay the normal late fee for films and games.
5. The late fee for a single item is never higher than 5 euros.
6. Items put into the return box while the library is closed count as returned on the next opening day.
7. Reserving an item costs 1 euro, which is paid when the reserved item is collected.
8. A lost library card is replaced for 3 euros.

Case: Mr Novak, 45 years old, borrowed a film on Tuesday, 4 March. He did not extend the loan. On Sunday, 16 March, in the evening, he put the film into the return box. How many euros does Mr Novak have to pay as a late fee?
base.note: due Tuesday 11 March; counts as returned on Tuesday 18 March; charged days: Wed 12, Thu 13, Fri 14, Sat 15, Tue 18 = 5 x 0.50; traps: 2.00 (return on Sunday), 3.50 (Sunday and Monday charged)

base.question:
On Monday the team of a small architecture office was told by e-mail that Thursday's client presentation would take place in the large meeting room on the second floor at 10:00. Everybody read that e-mail.

On Tuesday morning the office manager, Mrs Roth, learned that the large meeting room would be repainted on Thursday. She booked the library on the ground floor instead and announced the change at the Tuesday lunch meeting. Daniel, Farida and Olga were at that lunch. Ben was at the dentist, and Petra was on a train to a building site in Kassel, from where she came back late on Wednesday night; neither of them heard the announcement.

On Tuesday afternoon Farida met Ben at the coffee machine and told him about the new room. Ben thanked her and said: "Good to know, I would have gone upstairs." Nobody told Petra, because everybody assumed that somebody else had done it. Petra did not look at the room booking system; she never does.

On Wednesday afternoon Daniel and Farida carried the cardboard model of the building and the projector down to the library and tested the slides there. Ben helped them for a few minutes. Petra's desk stayed empty all day.

On Wednesday evening the painters called: they were ill and would come a week later. Mrs Roth, who was already at home, decided that it was too late to change everything again and left the booking as it was, so the presentation stays in the library. She sent no message to anybody.

On Thursday at 9:50 Olga, who had worked from home since Wednesday morning, phoned Daniel and asked whether there was anything new. Daniel said: "No, nothing has changed since Tuesday lunch." At 9:55 the client arrived at the reception desk, where Mrs Roth welcomed him.

To which place does Petra most likely go at 10:00 on Thursday for the presentation?
options: to the large meeting room on the second floor
to the library on the ground floor
to the building site in Kassel
base.answer: to the large meeting room on the second floor
base.note: Petra only knows Monday's e-mail; trap: the library (where the presentation really is)

base.question:
How to find the Clockwork Museum from the railway station. Leave the station through the main exit; when you step out of it you are facing south, and the taxi rank is directly in front of you. Walk straight ahead across the square to the fountain with the three stone fish. At the fountain turn left and walk along Baker Street, past the bakery with the blue awning and the bicycle shop, until you reach the traffic lights. There a tram line crosses your way; the trams run east and west, so do not be confused by them. At the traffic lights turn right and cross the old stone bridge over the river. Directly after the bridge the road bends sharply to the right, by a full quarter turn; simply follow the bend. Walk on until you see a church with a green tower on your left-hand side. At the church turn left into Lantern Lane. Most visitors now walk too far: after about a hundred metres you reach a flower shop, and that means you have missed the entrance to the alley. Turn around there and walk back about twenty metres. Now Tinsmith Alley branches off to your right; turn right into it. The alley is narrow and paved with cobblestones. At its end, on your left-hand side, is the museum. Turn left to face its red entrance door. The museum is open from ten to five and is closed on Mondays.

If you follow this description exactly, in which compass direction are you facing when you stand in front of the red entrance door and look at it?
base.note: south, left -> east, right -> south, bend right -> west, left -> south, turn around -> north, right -> east, left -> north; trap: skipping the turn-around gives south

base.question:
Ines travels from Lisbon to Helsinki to visit her brother. All times in her travel plan are local times. Lisbon time is one hour behind Frankfurt time, and Helsinki time is one hour ahead of Frankfurt time.

Her alarm clock rings at 4:30. The taxi comes at 5:15 and needs 25 minutes to the airport. Boarding for her first flight closes 20 minutes before departure, and her seat is 14C. Her first flight leaves Lisbon at 7:10 and takes 3 hours and 5 minutes to Frankfurt. In Frankfurt her plan allows 1 hour and 35 minutes between landing and the departure of her second flight. The second flight is scheduled to take 2 hours and 30 minutes to Helsinki. From Helsinki airport a train runs to the central station at 10 and at 40 minutes past every hour; the ride takes 30 minutes. Ines needs 45 minutes from the moment of landing until she stands on the train platform, because of the long walk and the luggage. Her brother lives ten minutes on foot from the central station.

On the day of the journey everything goes exactly as planned until Frankfurt. There the second flight takes off 50 minutes late, but it makes up 10 minutes in the air, so the flight is 10 minutes shorter than scheduled.

At what local time does Ines arrive at Helsinki central station? Answer as HH:MM.
base.note: lands in Frankfurt 11:15, departs 13:40, lands in Helsinki 17:00 local, on the platform 17:45, train 18:10, arrival 18:40; traps: 17:40 (time zones ignored or wrong train), 18:10

base.question:
On Sunday the Wilson family drove to Lake Arden for a picnic. On Saturday evening Emma had prepared everything: she made 12 cheese sandwiches and 8 ham sandwiches, wrapped each one in paper and put all of them into the big green cool box, together with 6 bottles of lemonade and a bag of 10 apples. She also packed paper plates, a knife, salt and a thermos flask of coffee into a wicker basket, which Noah carried to the car straight away. Her husband Noah put the picnic blanket, the football and the folding chairs into the boot of the car that same evening. On Sunday morning the children, Mia (9) and Leo (6), could not agree who was allowed to sit behind the driver, the cat escaped into the garden and had to be caught, and in the end the family left forty minutes later than planned. Emma carried the cool box as far as the hall, put it down next to the shoe cabinet in order to lock the terrace door, and then everybody got into the car and drove off; the cool box was still standing next to the shoe cabinet when they came home that evening.

The drive to the lake took 1 hour and 20 minutes. On the way Noah stopped at a petrol station and bought a newspaper and 4 chocolate bars. At the lake they found a nice place under an old oak tree, spread out the blanket and played football for a while. At half past twelve everybody was hungry. Mia said that she wanted 3 sandwiches, Leo wanted 2, and Noah announced that he could easily eat 5. They drank the coffee from the thermos flask, and a friendly family under the next tree gave the children 2 bananas. In the afternoon they swam, built a dam in the little stream and drove home at five o'clock.

How many of the sandwiches that Emma had made did the family eat at the lake?
base.note: the cool box with all the sandwiches stayed in the hall at home; trap: 10 (3 + 2 + 5)

base.question:
Ada and Ben play a simple board game. The track has squares numbered from 0 (start) to 60. Both pieces start on square 0. The players take turns; Ada begins, then Ben, then Ada again, and so on. The rules are:
(a) On your turn you roll one die and move your own piece forward by the number rolled.
(b) If you roll a 1, you do not move at all in that turn, and rules (c) and (d) do not apply.
(c) If your piece ends its move on a square whose number can be divided by 7 without remainder (7, 14, 21, ...), it immediately moves 3 further squares forward. This bonus is given at most once per turn.
(d) If your piece, after rules (a) and (c), stands on the same square as the other player's piece, the other player's piece is sent back to square 0. Square 0 itself is never a multiple of 7 for rule (c), and two pieces on square 0 do not affect each other.

The dice rolls of the game so far, in the order in which they were rolled, are: 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 5, 2, 4, 5, 5, 1, 1, 6. The first roll was Ada's.

On which square does Ada's piece stand after these rolls? Answer with the number of the square.
base.note: Ada: 2, 8, 12, sent back to 0 when Ben lands on 12, then 5, 9, 14 -> 17 (bonus), a rolled 1; Ben: 4, 9, 12, 14 -> 17, 22, a rolled 1, 28 -> 31; traps: forgetting the capture (29), the bonus or the rolled 1
